note: Every worksheet type → one teaching point → existing activities (covered) or a planned new instrument (backlog num). Regenerated only by hand-editing; checked by scripts/audit-activity-coverage.js.

points.skill: Count a set (scattered, framed, in an array) and name / write / match the number, to 10–20
points.note: The Counting Table (#14), Peek Window (#11), Fruit Crates (#7) and Jar Label (#6) count a set and name or write its number; array counting (K-027) is a structured layout of the same act. K-343 (count the family on ten-frames) is the same skill on personal content.

points.skill: Make a set of a given number (fill the frame, colour exactly N)
points.note: Animal Train (#9), Treat Box (#13) and Roll Book (#12) all count OUT a given number.

points.skill: One-to-one correspondence: give each one a partner
points.note: Partner Bows (#17) has the child make every pair; Twin Pools (#15) ties strings one for one.

points.skill: Compare two groups: more, fewer, equal (incl. comparing the letter counts of two names)
points.note: Partner Bows (#17) and Friendship Bridge (#18) cover more / fewer / same. K-346 (letters in my name vs a friend’s, from all-about-me) is the same comparison on personal content.

points.skill: Represent a count with tally marks (bundles of five) and read a tally back as a number
points.note: No activity uses tally marks; the five-bundle (four strokes and a crossing fifth) is a representation of its own, read by fives-and-ones.

points.skill: Odd or even by pairing up: one left over means odd
points.note: The existing even/odd row is a grade-2 numeral tap; the K sheet teaches the pairing STRATEGY (the leftover). Recommendation: when choice-board.even-odd reaches its ORDER rebuild, build it as a NEW pairing instrument (objects pair off two by two; the leftover one is the verdict) with a "pictures up to 10" setting for K. Not proposed separately here, to avoid two pairing instruments. Fully covered when ORDER row 137 (choice-board.even-odd.2-oa-c-3) is rebuilt to docs/activities-rebuild/rebuild-inputs/137-dealing-table.md.

points.skill: Subitize: recognise small quantities and dot / dice / frame arrangements at a glance
points.note: The Peek Window (#11, "the window that shows then hides") is a subitizing instrument with dice faces, five-and-some and pairs.

points.skill: Fill missing numbers in a count-along strip to 10 / 20 (count forward)
points.note: Peek Path (#2) and Constellation Thread (#3) count forward from a given number to 20.

points.skill: Name the number before / after / between, and count backward from 10
points.note: Every existing sequence instrument moves FORWARD only (the Peek Path even hints "count forward, not back"). "Before", "between" and the countdown are the backward direction no activity enacts.

points.skill: Join numbered dots in counting order (1–10, 11–20, count on from 11 to 30)
points.note: The Constellation Thread (#3) IS a dot-to-dot whose picture only exists if the count is right (to 20). K-296 runs to 30, past the activity’s 20 ceiling — a "to 30" round set would close it, not a new instrument.

points.skill: Trace and write the numerals 0–9 and 11–20
points.note: The Fading Line (#4) traces numerals along a guide; Jar Label (#6) writes 1–20.

points.skill: Ordinal numbers: find / name the 1st–10th in a line, counting from the marked end (either end)
points.note: Nothing teaches ordinal position; the two classic slips — counting from the wrong end, and marking three things instead of the third thing — are untouched.

points.skill: Estimate a quantity, then check by counting
points.note: The Bug Jar (#16).

points.skill: How many altogether: put two groups together and count all
points.note: ORDER rows 23–24 (not yet rebuilt) teach putting together on a ten frame.

points.skill: Number bonds: decompose numbers to 10 into two parts, find the missing part or the whole, make ten
points.note: Make 10 (K.OA.A.4) and three K.OA.A.3 decompose activities; missing-whole (K-276) is the grade-1 Find the Total bond.

points.skill: Number bonds to 20
points.note: A grade-1 skill on a K-filed sheet; grade-1 bond and make-a-ten activities teach it.

points.skill: Add and subtract fluently (within 5 / 10 / 20) — the colour-by-code math sheets
points.note: The math is quick facts; the colouring is only the answer channel (and the CBN decks already ship a tap-to-colour screen).

points.skill: Find the biggest / tallest / longest (and all the big ones) in a row, incl. shapes
points.note: Comparing Length (taller / shorter / longer) and Describe Attributes (ORDER rows 32, 34; not yet rebuilt).

points.skill: Seriate 3–5 pictures by size or height (smallest → biggest, shortest → tallest)
points.note: The Faraway Shelf (grade 1) compares ribbon LENGTHS against a cord; ordering 3–5 objects by overall height directly, at K, is missing. The Nesting Pots order NUMERALS, not objects.

points.skill: Compare weight: which is heavier / lighter, knowing that bigger is not always heavier
points.note: Describe Attributes names "heavy" as an attribute; nothing compares two weights. Capacity (Bramble) and length are covered, weight is not.

points.skill: Visual discrimination: find the identical twins, the pairs, and the one that differs (in detail, size or shape)
points.note: No activity trains looking for the EXACT same; the odd-one-out activity that exists is CATEGORY reasoning (Ziggy), not visual identity.

points.skill: Which one does not belong (by category)
points.note: Ziggy’s Odd One Out teaches exactly this (filed grade 1; comparable level).

points.skill: Repeating patterns AB / ABC / AABB by picture, size, position and shape — extend, fill the missing element — and growing patterns
points.note: Eight sheets and two deck apps (pattern-train, pattern-worksheet) — and not one activity. The Pattern Bench is a premium tool, not an activity; the activity catalogue has no patterning at all.

points.skill: Complete a picture grid: each row holds one kind; find the piece that fits the gap
points.note: Row / column reasoning (the K root of picture sudoku) has no activity; sudoku and grid-match exist only as deck apps.

points.skill: Match a picture to its shadow; recognise a whole picture from a part (visual closure)
points.note: Shadow-match is a deck app; no activity matches outline to object or part to whole.

points.skill: Recognise the mirror image (reflection) of a picture
points.note: Reflection is not taught anywhere; children confuse a mirror image with the same picture or a turned one.

points.skill: Search a busy scene for every one like the target (pictures, shapes; the shape of everyday objects)
points.note: Systematic search (not missing any, not marking twice) and finding shapes in real objects have no activity; find-objects / find-and-count are deck apps.

points.skill: Count each kind in a mixed scene (classify, then count)
points.note: Sort and Count (ORDER row 35).

points.skill: Compare two pictures and find what changed / what is missing
points.note: Already interactive: the b7 find-the-differences decks (242 + the 2,244-deck level set) each ship a tap-the-differences screen with a key; an activity would duplicate that screen. Careful visual comparison is also trained by the proposed pairing-pegs.

points.skill: Position words: on / under / beside, left / right, top / middle / bottom, inside / outside
points.note: The Parking Tower covers above / below / between (its floors give top / middle / bottom); on, under, beside, inside, outside and left / right are missing.

points.skill: Name 2D shapes in any orientation or proportion; follow a shape-coded key; count triangles and squares in a figure
points.note: Professor Pip’s Museum names shapes any way they turn; colour-by-shape-code is shape identification with a colouring answer channel.

points.skill: Count the sides of a shape; sort shapes by number of sides
points.note: Count the Sides (K) + Sort by Sides.

points.skill: Compose shapes from pieces (tangram figures; where two or three pieces meet)
points.note: Mim’s Glow Workshop fills a blank silhouette with pieces (filed grade 1; the K tangram is the same act with fewer pieces). A "2–3 pieces" round set would fit K exactly.

points.skill: Draw / build named shapes on dot paper (sides and corners)
points.note: Every shape activity NAMES or SORTS ready-made shapes; none has the child BUILD one from sides and corners.

points.skill: Match a side view to the view from above (the first map skill)
points.note: No map or perspective activity exists.

points.skill: Copy a picture square by square onto an empty grid (with and without letter–number labels)
points.note: Grid copying / first coordinates has no activity.

points.skill: Pre-writing strokes: lines, slants, zigzags, waves, loops, spirals, shapes, picture-to-picture paths
points.note: The Fading Line and the letter traces form numerals and letters; the strokes that come BEFORE letters (the pencil control itself) have no activity.

points.skill: Trace capital and lowercase letters A–Z
points.note: Penny’s Alphabet Trace and Snippy’s Letter Trace.

points.skill: Trace and copy whole words (first words, long words, capitals, sight words) and short sentences, left to right with spaces between words
points.note: Letters are traced one at a time; nothing teaches a WORD as a left-to-right run of letters, or the space between words in a sentence.

points.skill: Read sight words alone and in sentences; find a sight word among look-alikes
points.note: Read Common Sight Words + Tell the Words Apart. K-392 (colour every box with the word) is also served by the proposed search-lens "words" setting.

points.skill: Identify and sort by the beginning sound (letter of the week, m or n)
points.note: Beginning Sounds (ORDER row not yet rebuilt).

points.skill: Hear a sound at the beginning, middle or end; ending sounds; the middle vowel
points.note: Coco’s Sound Boxes: first, middle and last sounds.

points.skill: Segment a word into its sounds — one sound per box, count the sounds, two letters for one sound share one box
points.note: Coco’s Sound Boxes asks WHERE a sound is; the CVC builder spells three letters. Neither has the child push one token per sound (Elkonin) and count them, nor shows two letters sharing one sound.

points.skill: Match capital and small letters
points.note: Match Uppercase and Lowercase Letters.

points.skill: Find every copy of a letter among look-alikes (b / d / p / q); circle and count a letter inside words
points.note: Letter-case matching pairs two forms of one letter; picking a letter out of its mirror-twins and out of words is a search the catalogue lacks.

points.skill: Alphabetical order: fill the missing letters, join dots a to t
points.note: No activity teaches the order of the alphabet (alphabet-train is a deck app).

points.skill: Build / complete CVC words from letters
points.note: Build the CVC Word.

points.skill: Match a word to the picture it names (picture-word cards, memory pairs)
points.note: Read the Word, Tap the Picture + Bingo’s Word Hunt.

points.skill: Tell vowels from consonants
points.note: Nothing names vowels as a class of letters.

points.skill: Hear rhymes: rhyming pairs, rhyme or not
points.note: Rosa Raccoon’s Rhyme Wagon.

points.skill: Count the syllables in a word; sort pictures by syllable count
points.note: The Syllable Builder BLENDS given syllables into a word; clapping out and counting the syllables of a picture word is the other half of RF.K.2.b and is missing.

points.skill: Hear the digraph (sh / ch) at the start of a word
points.note: Build Blend and Digraph Words (grade 1) teaches digraph words; the K face is a listening sort on the same content.

points.skill: One and many: singular and plural nouns
points.note: Daisy’s Plate Stack.

points.skill: Choose the article for a noun (en a / an; de der / die / das; fr le / la …)
points.note: No activity teaches articles in any locale.

points.skill: Match opposites with pictures
points.note: Quill’s Mirror Market.

points.skill: Sort pictures into two or more groups by category (incl. cut-and-paste sorts)
points.note: Mim’s Memory Baskets.

points.skill: Recognise feelings in faces, match face to feeling word, comfortable vs uncomfortable feelings, name how I feel
points.note: No SEL activity exists.

points.skill: Days of the week in order; fill the missing days
points.note: No calendar activity.

points.skill: The four seasons: sort pictures and clothes by season, the seasons in order (the cycle), what does not belong, a tree through the year
points.note: No seasons activity.

points.skill: Weather symbols and words; a week of weather; cold / warm / hot on a thermometer; hot and cold things
points.note: No weather activity.

points.skill: Day and night: what belongs to the day sky and to the night
points.note: No sky activity. Served by the weather-window "sky" setting (the same window, a sun / moon dial) but kept a separate teaching point.

points.skill: Put story pictures in order (first, next, last)
points.note: Wake Up, Pip! retells a story in order; Dot’s Story Spine names start / trouble / fix. NOTE: id "c" in types-K.txt is K-379-story-sequencing (the dump regex mis-read its id).

points.skill: Healthy habits: hand-washing steps in order; which tool for which body-care job (toothbrush, soap, comb, tissue)
points.note: No health activity.

points.skill: Read the traffic light / pedestrian signal and cross the road in the right steps (stop, look, listen, cross)
points.note: No safety activity.

points.skill: The five senses: which body part we use for each experience
points.note: No senses activity.

points.skill: Parts of the body: name and label them, how many of each, which come in twos, what is missing
points.note: No body activity. K-344 (label the face, from all-about-me) is the same labelling skill on the face.

points.skill: Living and non-living things
points.note: No life-science activity.

points.skill: Natural or made by people
points.note: No materials activity.

points.skill: Fruits and vegetables (which part of the plant we eat)
points.note: Mim’s Baskets sorts foods with foods; the fruit / vegetable distinction (and why) is not taught.

points.skill: Everyday foods and sometimes foods
points.note: No nutrition activity.

points.skill: Pets, farm and wild animals; where animals live (animal homes)
points.note: No habitat activity at K.

points.skill: Animal babies and their parents (alike and different)
points.note: No offspring / life-cycle activity.

points.skill: Land, water and air transport; things that fly
points.note: No transport activity.

points.skill: Wants and needs
points.note: No economics activity.

points.skill: Community helpers and the tools they use
points.note: No community-helper activity.

points.skill: Recycling: which bin each finished thing goes in
points.note: No recycling activity.

points.skill: What plants need to grow (water and light)
points.note: No plant-science activity.

points.skill: Things that float and things that sink
points.note: No sink / float activity.

points.skill: Family members and family words (mother, grandfather, brother …) on a family tree
points.note: No family activity. NOTE: id "ego" in types-K.txt is K-370-family (the dump regex caught the word "ego" in its header comment).

points.skill: All about me: self-portrait, my favourite things, things I can do (personal expression)
points.note: Open-ended personal expression (draw yourself, pick YOUR favourite, tick what YOU can do) has no single right answer, which the activity law requires; the countable faces of the family (K-343, K-346) and the labelling face (K-344) are mapped to their skills.

points.skill: Bilingual picture word cards for a word wall
points.note: A print artefact (cut-out cards in two languages for the classroom wall); the reading skill is covered by word-picture-match, and every activity already ships in 11 locales.

points.skill: Draw a picture step by step (simple shapes, trace then draw, finish the drawing, draw and write)
points.note: Free drawing has no checkable answer and no drawing recognition is available; the pencil control it practises is covered by the proposed pencil-path, shape composing by shapeforge.

points.skill: Colour by number / colour pictures and scenes by a numeral key
points.note: Already interactive: the CBN decks (2,200 + b7) ship a tap-to-colour screen with a key. Numeral recognition itself is covered by Letterbox Street / Jar Label.

points.skill: Mazes and handmade picture mazes (incl. ABC, lowercase, numbers 1–20, beginning-sound and babies-and-mothers routes, maze colouring)
points.note: Already interactive: every maze deck (b8 maze-puzzles, mzl level set) ships a trace-path "draw the way" screen with a key. The content inside the themed faces is covered by its own skill: alphabet order (alphabet-lockers), numbers to 20 (constellation), beginning sounds (choice-board.beginning-sound), mothers and babies (mother-and-baby).

points.skill: Add two groups within 10-12 using a picture, ten-frame, domino or dice model
points.note: Join-two-groups with a model is taught by the ten-frame operation activity and the find-the-total bond (within 20). Domino/dice faces are a subitising dress of the same skill.

points.skill: Subtract within 10 by crossing out (take-away) a picture model
points.note: Take-away on a ten frame is the same model as crossing out pictures.

points.skill: Find the partner that makes 10 (number bonds to 10)
points.note: G1-427 is the make-10 maze (pairs that make 10 open the way): same skill; the maze dress already has the deck trace screen.

points.skill: Add three groups / three numbers
Use three related numbers to write the four facts of a fact family (addition and subtraction are inverse)
points.note: Existing activities do commutativity and subtraction-as-unknown-addend one fact at a time; nothing makes the child produce ALL FOUR facts from one whole and two parts, or shows why 3 - 8 cannot be built from them. New instrument.

points.skill: Find the unknown in an addition/subtraction equation within 10/20 (pictures or numbers)
Add and subtract within 20 mentally (fluency, make-a-ten strategy)
points.note: G1-428 is the subtraction-within-20 maze; the skill is the same.

points.skill: Add and subtract by counting on / back with hops on a number line; count back from 20
points.note: Hopper hops forward to add and back to take away; at its rebuild it must keep a within-20 setting so the grade-1 faces stay covered. G1-294 (dot-to-dot counting back from 20) is the backward count sequence, practised in the back hops.

points.skill: Solve add/subtract word problems within 10/20 using pictures
Number walls: each brick is the sum of the two below; find a missing brick by subtracting; work top-down
points.note: No activity has the additive pyramid structure (sums of adjacent pairs, the inverse to find a missing base brick).

points.skill: Doubles and halves of a group / number to 20
points.note: Doubles are the named grade-1 fact strategy and no activity doubles or halves a set; fractions.partition-equal-shares halves SHAPES, not quantities.

points.skill: Odd and even: share a group fairly between two / circle in pairs; is anything left over?
points.note: The existing activity is a numeral quiz (tap even/odd); the grade-1 faces teach WHY: pairing / sharing a set and seeing the one left over. New instrument. Fully covered when ORDER row 137 (choice-board.even-odd.2-oa-c-3) is rebuilt to docs/activities-rebuild/rebuild-inputs/137-dealing-table.md.

points.skill: Read and build two-digit numbers as tens and ones (rods and cubes); expanded form
Represent one number many ways (tens/ones, ten frame, tally, 10 more/less, number words)
points.note: Each box on the page is a skill an existing activity teaches; the routine itself (one number, many faces) is a teacher routine served by the Number Talk Easel tool.

points.skill: Find 1 more / 1 less and 10 more / 10 less than a number
points.note: 1 less is only implicit in next-number; the hundreds-chart proposal (chart-patches) also enacts +/-1 and +/-10 physically.

points.skill: Skip count by 2s, 5s and 10s, with equal groups (running total) and on a number line whose ticks are worth 5 or 10
points.note: skipcount hops by 5/10/100 on numerals only and Posy counts tens; counting by 2s is missing, and nothing ties the count-by to equal GROUPS of objects or to reading ticks worth 5 or 10.

points.skill: Hundreds-chart structure: missing numbers, puzzle pieces (+1 right, +10 down), find the wrong number, colour a counting pattern
points.note: Track Repair is a number LINE; nothing shows the ten-wide grid where one step down means +10.

points.skill: Locate / read a number on a number line from the nearest printed number (0-10, 0-20 sparse labels, 0-30, 0-50, 20-40)
points.note: Track Repair places numbered ties by counting on from anchor stations: the exact skill. Ticks worth 5/10 are in the skip-counting point.

points.skill: Compare two-digit numbers (and picture groups) with > < =, and order three numbers least-to-greatest / greatest-to-least
points.note: The existing two-digit compare is a symbol quiz and the Nesting Pots order only 1-10. Missing: ordering two-digit numbers and the TENS-FIRST rule made visible (the 29 > 41 misconception). Fully covered when ORDER row 95 (choice-board.compare-two-digit.1-nbt-b-3) is rebuilt to docs/activities-rebuild/rebuild-inputs/95-ten-rod-drawers.md.

points.skill: Read and write number words to 20, tens words to 100, words to 50; match numerals to words
points.note: No activity reads or builds number names; the morphology (teen vs -ty; de/da/nl ones-before-tens, fr/da vigesimal names) is the real difficulty.

points.skill: Measure length with unit cubes/squares and order three objects by length
Tell time to the hour and half hour; match analog to digital
Draw (set) the clock hands for o'clock, half past, quarter hours, five minutes, mixed
points.note: Dragging the hands is the screen form of drawing them.

points.skill: Count coins in a purse (one kind, two kinds, all coins) and compare two purses
points.note: Comparing two purses is counting both totals; at rebuild keep a one-coin-kind first setting for grade 1.

points.skill: Read a bar graph, find the tallest bar, colour a bar graph from counts
points.note: Pip's Stacking Fence builds and reads bar graphs for up to four categories; grade 1 is three categories.

points.skill: Sort a mixed set into a table, read a picture graph (one picture per thing), find the most, how many more
points.note: Sort-and-count stops at a count; the bar graph starts from counts. Missing: organising real objects one per cell into a picture graph and reading the overhang as "how many more".

points.skill: Name 2D shapes, tell real from not-real by defining attributes, shape riddles
Compose figures from tangram pieces; find the missing piece
points.note: Mim's Glow Workshop composes shapes from pieces; a tangram-piece setting is worth considering at its rebuild.

points.skill: Complete a repeating pattern with two missing items
points.note: No activity teaches repeating patterns (Pattern Bench is a tool, not an activity).

points.skill: Picture analogies: A is to B as C is to ?
points.note: No activity reasons about a relation and transfers it to a new pair.

points.skill: 4x4 picture sudoku: every row, column and box has each picture once
points.note: The sudoku app ships decks, but no activity teaches the constraint reasoning.

points.skill: Logic grid with picture clues (cross out / circle what each child has)
points.note: Elimination reasoning is untaught by any activity.

points.skill: Sort pictures into three groups
Copy a picture square by square onto an empty grid (visual-spatial, row/column tracking)
points.note: No activity practises cell-by-cell copying; separate from the freehand drawing faces.

points.skill: Follow drawing steps, draw a figure in a scene, order drawing steps, copy each step
points.note: Freehand drawing with a pencil; the screen has no drawing recognition, and the one transferable part (copying on a grid) is the grid-copy point. Ordering steps (G1-418) is sequencing, practised by the story-sequencing activities.

points.skill: Visual discrimination: find 7 differences, how many differences, what changed (tick the words), mirror differences
points.note: Every find-the-differences deck already ships a tap-the-differences screen with an answer key (b7 flagship, interactive printable family); an activity would duplicate it.

points.skill: Picture mazes: big picture, underground, shortest way in town, tangled lines, collect the carrots, avoid the walruses
points.note: Every handmade-maze deck already ships a draw-the-way (trace-path) screen with per-face hints (b8); an activity would duplicate it. The maze faces with a content skill (G1-426 ABC, G1-427 make 10, G1-428 subtraction) are placed under those skills.

points.skill: Spell picture words (with first letter, word bank, letter boxes, plain lines)
points.note: Letter-tile building is the screen form of writing the word (no handwriting recognition needed).

points.skill: Put words in ABC order by first letter, and by second letter when the first is the same; hop the letters in order
points.note: No activity orders words alphabetically; the alphabet-train app is preschool letter order only.

points.skill: Clap and split words into syllables, missing syllable, syllable scramble, 2 or 3 syllables, syllable cards
points.note: G1-313 combines syllables and phonemes; the phoneme half is the phoneme-boxes point.

points.skill: Every syllable has a vowel (find the vowel in each syllable)
points.note: No activity names the rule that makes a syllable split checkable.

points.skill: Read word-family / syllable words (carpet), join syllables, words with blends, read syllabified words and find the picture
Segment a word into its sounds (sound boxes) and blend sounds into a word
points.note: At Coco's Sound Boxes rebuild keep a full-segmentation (every box, with blends) setting for grade 1.

points.skill: Consonant digraphs sh/ch/th: hear the letter team, write it, read and match, where in the word; sound of the week
points.note: "Build Blend and Digraph Words" builds sh/ch/th words; position is Coco's first/middle/last boxes.

points.skill: Hear, sort, finish and produce rhymes
points.note: Producing your own rhymes (G1-346) is free writing; the hearing/matching skill is covered.

points.skill: Put scrambled words into a sentence with a capital and an end mark
Sort nouns by the article in front (a/an; der/die/das; en/ett; un/une ...)
points.note: No activity teaches articles; in 10 of the 11 locales this is grammatical gender, a core grade-1 point.

points.skill: Nouns vs verbs; nouns vs adjectives
points.note: Only grade-2 adjectives/adverbs exist; nothing separates nouns from verbs or nouns from adjectives with a test the child can run.

points.skill: Opposites: write / pair / choose the opposite, opposites in a sentence
Two words, one picture: words that mean the same
points.note: Shades of meaning orders near-synonyms by strength; no activity tests SAME meaning.

points.skill: Order words from weakest to strongest
Find the word built from a root (picture word)
Fill the blank in a sentence from a word bank / choose the word / match the sentence to the picture
Personal pronouns: replace a name, sort names into he/she/they
Who / what / where: choose, fill in, match question to answer, sort answers
Read a sentence and do exactly what it says: colour N pictures a colour, two-step instructions, by place (first/second/between), true or false, read and draw
points.note: Existing activities check that a sentence makes sense or pick a picture; none makes the child EXECUTE a sentence with a number, a colour and a noun (exactly 3, not all of them). Read-and-draw (G1-342) is freehand; only its reading half transfers.

points.skill: Ordinal numbers: write the missing ordinals, match ordinal words, which place, who wins the race
points.note: No activity teaches 1st/2nd/3rd, or that the count starts from the front of the line.

points.skill: Yesterday/today/tomorrow, months in order, month before/after, day abbreviations, months and seasons
points.note: No calendar activity exists at any grade.

points.skill: Sequence a story: what happens next, draw the middle, order sentences to pictures
points.note: Drawing the middle (G1-401) is freehand; choosing/ordering the middle event is covered by the story spine.

points.skill: Classify animals into groups (mammal, bird, fish, reptile, insect) by body covering (fur, feathers, scales, smooth skin)
points.note: No science activity exists at grade 1.

points.skill: Where animals live, who does not live here, what animals eat, what animals need (food and a home)
Life cycles in order: chicken, butterfly, frog, plant; what comes next
Predict and test sink or float; heavier does not mean it sinks (balance scale)
points.note: "draw" in types-1.txt is the parse of G1-399 (file G1-399-sink-or-float.js, slug sink-or-float-experiment). The G1-204 bank once listed a plastic spoon as "sink": the object bank needs its own pedagogy check.

points.skill: Sort foods into the four food groups
Which sense for each thing: sort by sense, choose the body part, odd one out, write the sense word, I can hear / see ...
points.note: G1-361 asks for the child's own sentences; the identification skill transfers, the free writing does not.

points.skill: Name the parts of the body (label the figure)
Weather symbols and words; read a weekly forecast
What is it made of (paper, plastic, glass, metal, wood); things I recycle
points.note: G1-365 (draw three things you recycle) is personal drawing; the material identification transfers.

points.skill: Sun, Earth or Moon facts; moon phases in order (growing / shrinking)
Name the parts of a plant (root, stem, leaf, flower) and what each does
Read a map key: find each symbol on the map and count them
Road safety: traffic signs and what they mean
Family generations oldest to youngest; read clues to fill a family tree; my own family tree
points.note: G1-387 is a personal template (draw your people): the generation structure transfers, the personal drawing does not.

points.skill: Brushing teeth before/during/after; stop the germs (the healthy choice); weekly habit chart
points.note: G1-405 is a personal tracker for home; the choose-the-healthy-way and sequence skills transfer.

points.skill: Add two groups of base-ten blocks within 1000 and write the total
points.note: Tuck adds block groups with and without composing; the no-regrouping sheet is the easy end of the same model.

points.skill: Take away base-ten blocks within 1000
points.note: Same block model, take-away direction.

points.skill: Bundle 10 ones into a ten and read tens and ones
points.note: Bundle Bot is exactly circle-ten-ones-make-a-ten.

points.skill: Skip count by 5s, 10s and 100s (incl. the dot-to-dot and maze practice formats)
points.note: The dot-to-dot and the maze are formats of the same counting sequence; Hopper's Lily Hops covers 5s/10s/100s.

points.skill: Skip count by 3s and by 4s and fill the missing numbers
points.note: Hopper only steps 5/10/100, the friendly steps; 3s and 4s cross tens irregularly and are the multiplication-readiness skill.

points.skill: Count equal groups, write the repeated addition, then the multiplication sentence
points.note: Equal-groups model + reading a times sentence as groups.

points.skill: Rows and columns of an array; match an array to a multiplication
points.note: Build an Array covers rows x columns; Echo Grove covers picking the picture that matches a sentence.

points.skill: Share a pile equally into bins; count how many equal groups (division readiness)
points.note: Maple's Bakery does both sharing and grouping.

points.skill: Decide odd/even by pairing objects, as two equal addends (n + n or n + n + 1), and by the ones digit for numbers under 100
points.note: The existing board taps an even/odd label for a numeral; the standard's core (pair the objects, write as two equal addends, and WHY only the ones digit decides) is missing. Fully covered when ORDER row 137 (choice-board.even-odd.2-oa-c-3) is rebuilt to docs/activities-rebuild/rebuild-inputs/137-dealing-table.md.

points.skill: Compare two 3-digit numbers with < > = and order four from smallest to greatest
points.note: Only a match-pairs card game for comparing two; nothing makes "compare the hundreds first" physical and nothing orders four. Fully covered when ORDER row 151 (match-pairs.compare-three-digit-numbers.2-nbt-a-4) is rebuilt to docs/activities-rebuild/rebuild-inputs/151-three-door-tunnel.md.

points.skill: Round to the nearest ten on a number line and by the 5-or-more rule
points.note: Halfway Harbors sends a boat to the nearest round number.

points.skill: Read and build a 3-digit number from hundreds/tens/ones blocks and a place-value chart
points.note: Same model; the chart is a readout the activity already shows.

points.skill: Expanded form of a 3-digit number and the value of a digit
points.note: Expanded form shows each digit as its place value.

points.skill: Find 100 more and 100 less
Partition shapes into halves, thirds and fourths; recognise equal vs unequal parts; match a picture to its fraction
points.note: G2-231 prints 1/2-style notation (3.NF.A.1); the shape-partition skill is covered, the symbol is reached by fox-forge at grade 3.

points.skill: Find a fraction (1/2, 1/3, 1/4) of a set of pictures and say how many that is
points.note: Sharing is covered, but "one third of 12 is 4" (one share of an equal split of a SET, not a shape) is not.

points.skill: Measure an object with a ruler starting at 0
Measure two objects and find how much longer
Make a bar graph from a tally/data set and answer put-together and compare questions
points.note: Pip's Stacking Fence builds bars a unit at a time and asks how-many-more; the tally is only the data source.

points.skill: Read and make a pictograph where each picture stands for 2
points.note: No activity has a scaled key; children count pictures as ones.

points.skill: Read a line plot (X marks above numbers)
Sort 2D shapes by number of sides
Count the faces, edges and vertices of cubes, prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones
points.note: Only flat-vs-solid exists; nothing counts the parts of a solid, where the classic error is counting only the visible faces/edges.

points.skill: Match a solid (sphere, cube, cylinder, cone, rectangular prism, pyramid) to a real object of the same shape
points.note: Pip's Museum names flat shapes; nothing links solids to everyday objects. Served by the ink-pad instrument's "real objects" setting (the prints prove the match).

points.skill: Sort shapes into flat (2D) and solid (3D)
points.note: The Kindergarten activity teaches this exact distinction.

points.skill: Decide whether a dashed line is a mirror line; pick the picture that is the same on both sides
points.note: No symmetry activity at any grade.

points.skill: Complete a half-drawn grid picture so it is symmetrical (vertical and horizontal mirror lines)
points.note: Same apparatus as symmetry-line ("complete" setting); a teacher teaches identify and complete as two lessons, so two points, one instrument.

points.skill: Tell time to 5 minutes and to the quarter hour
Add and subtract 2- and 3-digit numbers in columns, ones first, writing the carried/borrowed digit
points.note: Tuck regroups BLOCKS; nothing teaches the written column layout (digits aligned in place columns, start at the ones, the little carried 1 written above the tens) that all six sheets drill.

points.skill: Read the liquid in a measuring jug in millilitres (to 1000 and 2000 ml)
points.note: Pippa's Pond-Juice Lab pours and reads a scale; the 2000 ml jug is a range, not a new skill.

points.skill: Read mass in grams on a balance with weights and on a scale with small steps (incl. the mixed jug + scale sheets)
points.note: Jugs are covered by Pond-Juice; mass on a balance (the sum of weights that levels the beam) and reading a scale with small steps are taught nowhere. The two mixed sheets sit here because their missing half is mass.

points.skill: Add up shelf prices, decide whether there is enough money, find how much more, and make change
points.note: Change and paying a target with coins are covered; totalling a basket of 2-3 prices and comparing money with a price ("enough? how much more?") carry most of these 8 sheets and have no apparatus.

points.skill: Read a month calendar: weekday of a date, one week later, days between two dates
points.note: No calendar activity exists.

points.skill: Find a square by its letter-number code (B2) and colour it; write the code of a square
points.note: Position words exist; coordinate codes do not.

points.skill: Locate a number on a number line that starts at 40 or 60 and labels only some ticks
points.note: Existing lines label every tie or start at 0; counting on from the nearest label in a sparse window of the line is missing.

points.skill: Add/subtract within 100 in puzzle formats: number walls and the math maze
points.note: The wall and the maze are formats; the skill (sums and missing parts within 100) is covered.

points.skill: Move on a hundreds chart (down = 10 more, right = 1 more); find a square from two arrow paths; count the jumps between two numbers
points.note: 10 more/less is covered as mental maths; the CHART STRUCTURE (rows of ten, a column = +10) and composite moves/differences are not.

points.skill: Solve a logic grid from yes/no/either-or clues (cross out what cannot be, check what must be) and read a solved grid
points.note: No deduction activity exists.

points.skill: Match a tangram solution to its shadow exactly, rejecting turned or flipped ones
points.note: Shapeforge composes shapes from blocks but never demands a fixed orientation or tells a flip from a turn.

points.skill: Read a short story and answer who/what/where/when/why with details from the text
points.note: K key details (3-picture stories) and grade-1 trait evidence exist; a grade-2 multi-paragraph story where each answer must be anchored in a found sentence does not.

points.skill: Capital letter and end mark; choose . or ?; split two run-together sentences
points.note: Capitalising NAMES and grammar repair exist; where a sentence ends (and that the next word then takes a capital) has no apparatus.

points.skill: Sort words into nouns, verbs and adjectives (with and without picture help)
points.note: Glim covers adjective vs adverb only; noun/verb/adjective classification is missing.

points.skill: Write sentences about a picture using a word bank and sentence starters
points.note: Sentence Builder unscrambles GIVEN words; nothing asks the child to compose a TRUE sentence about what a picture shows. Free handwriting cannot be read, so the instrument composes from tiles.

points.skill: Retell a picture story in order with time-order starters (First, Next, Then, At the end)
points.note: Retelling exists at K; ordering the events AND choosing the time-order word each frame needs is the grade-2 writing skill.

points.skill: Apply a position-dependent spelling rule (e.g. ck/k, tch/ch, -dge/-ge, ai/ay; -s/-es/-ies plurals): fill, spot and sort by the rule letters
points.note: Spell-by-ear and irregular plurals exist; a rule that picks the spelling by its POSITION in the word is taught nowhere.

points.skill: Build, split and mean compound words (incl. the joining letter in de/nl/sv/da/no)
points.note: Skip's Word-Welding Yard builds and means compounds; the joining-letter face is a locale detail of the same skill.

points.skill: Present and past forms incl. irregular be/have/do/go; choose the form for a sentence; find the verb
points.note: The types file parsed the id of G2-317 as "ls" (file G2-317-verb-forms.js).

points.skill: Add a prefix to change meaning (un-, dis-, in-; re-, pre-, mis-)
points.note: Marigold's Knowing Machine applies prefixes for meaning.

points.skill: Write the plural for more than one (regular and irregular)
Use the story context to choose the missing word
Link a pronoun to its name; possessive pronouns; replace a name with a pronoun
points.note: The Borrowed Hat covers personal and possessive pronouns.

points.skill: Choose/write the question word that asks for a highlighted answer (who, where, why, how)
points.note: Same skill at K level (Wren's set includes why/how).

points.skill: Match words that mean the same; pick a synonym for "said"
points.note: Shades of meaning (said -> whispered/shouted) is covered; "means the same" as a TEST of meaning is not. The types file parsed the id of G2-358 as "ls" (file G2-358-synonyms.js).

points.skill: Find the shared root word; sort words by root
Find and count a digraph (sh) in sentences
points.note: Build Blend and Digraph Words.

points.skill: Write cursive lowercase letters, capitals, the joins between letters, and whole words
points.note: Print-letter tracing exists; joined (cursive) writing does not.

points.skill: Read words written in cursive
points.note: Served by the cursive instrument's "read" setting.

points.skill: Gather true facts about an animal into a fact file (eats, lives, moves, body covering, babies)
points.note: Atlas reads ONE fact for a key detail; organising facts under headings (the research-writing skill) is missing.

points.skill: Compare two animals: which facts are the same and which are different
points.note: Comparing two STORIES exists; comparing two sets of facts does not. Served by the fact-cabinet two-animal setting.

points.skill: Use clues one at a time to find a mystery animal
points.note: No clue-by-clue inference activity.

points.skill: Name plant parts, what each part does, and which part of a plant we eat
Order the butterfly life cycle and match young stages to the animal they become
Day and night come from the Earth turning toward or away from the Sun
Name the phases of the Moon
points.note: Served by the orbit-lamp Moon setting; taught as its own lesson.

points.skill: The four compass directions and using them on a map
Name and locate the continents on a world map
Kinds of road signs (warning / must-not / information) and which sign fits a situation
Family words for relationships (aunt, cousin, grandmother) from riddles
Why we do healthy habits (what each habit protects)
Which animals and plants live in a habitat, and which body feature helps an animal live there
points.note: Category sorting exists; habitat fit by adaptation does not.

points.skill: Predict and test sink or float; changing shape (a clay boat) changes floating
Group things by the material they are made of (paper, plastic, glass, metal, wood) for recycling
points.note: Odd-one-out by category exists; by MATERIAL (a property, not a category) does not.

points.skill: Visual discrimination: find 10 differences; write a sentence about each difference
points.note: Every find-the-differences deck already ships its own tap-the-differences screen + key (b7 / fd level set), so an activity would duplicate it; the writing half of G2-389 is the describe-a-picture skill (true-caption).

points.skill: Draw by steps then write about it; draw from memory
points.note: Free drawing cannot be checked on screen and its targets are fine motor (covered by the tracing activities and cursive-ribbon) and visual memory; the write-three-sentences half is the describe-a-picture skill (true-caption).

points.skill: Interpret a product as equal groups / an array and find the total
points.note: Echo Grove reads a×b as a groups of b and refuses the same-total look-alike; Build an Array covers big arrays up to 10×10 by rows.

points.skill: Multiply as equal jumps from 0 on a number line (multiples)
points.note: Hopper's hops add/subtract with mixed lengths and Lily Hops skip-counts only by 5/10/100; nothing lays b equal jumps of any size 2-10 and reads the landing as a×b.

points.skill: Divide by sharing a pile equally into a given number of groups
points.note: Maple's Bakery shares cookies equally onto plates (partitive) and packs boxes (quotative).

points.skill: Divide by measuring: how many equal hops back from N reach 0
points.note: Maple's packing mode is quotative with objects, but no activity shows division as repeated subtraction on a number line. Same rod instrument as mult-number-line, run backwards (setting: lay out / measure back) — multiplication and division are the two directions of one apparatus, each a separate round set.

points.skill: Find an unknown factor and write the four related facts (division as an unknown-factor problem)
points.note: Multiplication and division are each covered alone; nothing makes one array carry all four facts or makes the child find the missing side of a known total.

points.skill: Area of a rectangle = rows × columns (tiling becomes multiplication)
points.note: The two area activities count unit squares one by one; the step 3.MD.C.7 names (the tiling as rows of equal length, multiplied) is not taught.

points.skill: a×b and b×a give the same total (turn the array)
points.note: Echo Grove deliberately treats 3×4 and 4×3 as different groupings; no activity shows they have the same product.

points.skill: Name and shade a/b as a copies of the unit piece 1/b
points.note: Pip's Chocolate Forge builds a/b from a chosen unit piece; naming (315) and shading (316) are the two directions of that same act.

points.skill: Place a fraction on a number line from 0 to 1 by counting equal spaces
points.note: No activity puts fractions on a number line.

points.skill: Recognise equivalent fractions as the same amount
points.note: Crumb's Same-Amount Bakery picks the piece showing the same amount cut a different way.

points.skill: Compare two fractions of the same whole (same numerator or same denominator)
points.note: Only equality is taught; bigger/smaller, the 'bigger denominator = bigger fraction' error and the same-whole condition are missing.

points.skill: Find a fraction of a group of objects (1/3 of 12)
points.note: All fraction activities use area models; none treats a set of objects as the whole.

points.skill: Rebuild the whole from one unit-fraction piece
points.note: The forge starts from a drawn whole; reasoning backwards from one piece to the whole is not taught.

points.skill: Partition shapes into equal areas and name each part as a unit fraction
points.note: Equal shares that look different and partition into thirds cover recognising equal areas.

points.skill: Round to the nearest 10 and 100 (number line, halfway, up/down)
points.note: The Halfway Harbors sends a boat to its nearest round-number harbour with the halfway buoy shown; the worksheet faces (sort up/down, which round to 50, round twice) are the same skill. Check at rebuild that its pool includes nearest-100 rounds.

points.skill: Round both addends, add the rounded numbers, and judge whether an exact answer is reasonable
points.note: Rounding and exact adding are taught apart; using rounding to estimate a sum and check reasonableness is not.

points.skill: Compare four-digit numbers by place value from the left
points.note: Compare activities stop at three digits and match symbols; nothing shows that the first differing place decides (2,999 vs 3,001). Fully covered when ORDER row 151 (match-pairs.compare-three-digit-numbers.2-nbt-a-4) is rebuilt to docs/activities-rebuild/rebuild-inputs/151-three-door-tunnel.md.

points.skill: Find the constant step of a growing or shrinking number pattern (incl. 25s, 50s, 100s) and continue it
points.note: Skip-counting hands the child the step; finding an unknown step, shrinking patterns and steps of 25/50 are missing.

points.skill: Find the rule of an input/output machine and apply it both ways
points.note: No function-machine activity exists.

points.skill: Predict whether a sum is odd or even from the addends' parity, without adding
points.note: Even or Odd? classifies a single number; the pattern odd+odd=even etc. is not taught.

points.skill: Read and build scaled bar graphs and pictographs (one picture/step = 2, 5, 10)
points.note: Pip's Stacking Fence builds bar graphs at scale 1; the scale (each brick worth 5), which is the whole of 3.MD.B.3, is missing.

points.skill: Measure to the half unit and show the data on a line plot marked in halves
points.note: Shelly's Tide-Line uses whole units only; halves on the ruler and the plot are missing.

points.skill: Find perimeter as the distance around a shape
points.note: The Mending Fences counts the edge and separates fence from grass.

points.skill: Recognise rectangles with the same area but a different shape
points.note: The Mosaic Menders finds the mosaic with the same tile count against a bigger look-alike.

points.skill: Same perimeter, different area (and the reverse)
points.note: Mending Fences measures one fence at a time; the 3.MD.D.8 clause 'same perimeter, different areas' is not shown.

points.skill: Classify quadrilaterals by attributes; squares are rectangles (and rhombuses)
points.note: Sort by Sides stops at 'quadrilateral'; the nested categories (a square is a rectangle) are not taught.

points.skill: Recognise right angles (and angles smaller/bigger than a square corner)
points.note: No angle activity exists.

points.skill: Find and count lines of symmetry
points.note: No symmetry activity exists.

points.skill: Find how much time passed between two clock times
points.note: Both clock-elapsed activities give a start and a duration and ask for the end; the inverse (start + end -> duration) is not taught.

points.skill: Read an analog clock to the minute
points.note: Sprocket's Clock to the minute, with minute marks.

points.skill: Convert between 12-hour and 24-hour time
points.note: Covered at grade 2 at a comparable level.

points.skill: Add or subtract minutes/hours to a clock time
points.note: Count on / count back minutes on the clock.

points.skill: Read a thermometer whose scale counts by 2, 5 or 10
points.note: Pippa's lab reads a vertical liquid scale in mL; temperature, a scale that counts by 2s, and below-zero are missing.

points.skill: Count unit cubes in a solid, including hidden ones (volume)
points.note: No volume activity; the hidden-cube count is the essential part.

points.skill: Solve a 6×6 picture sudoku: each picture once in every row, column and box
points.note: Sudoku exists as interactive catalogue decks (the sudoku app), not as an activity; no activity teaches the once-per-line constraint.

points.skill: Complete a magic square so every row and column has the same sum
points.note: No activity reasons with several sums at once.

points.skill: The equal sign means both sides are the same amount; find the missing number with an operation on both sides
points.note: Numbers Court judges equations within 20 at grade 1; an unknown with expressions on BOTH sides (8+4=_+5) at grade-3 sizes is missing.

points.skill: Classify by two attributes at once (two-circle Venn, row × column table, the missing cell)
points.note: Every sort activity uses one attribute; the overlap (belongs to both) and the crossed table are missing.

points.skill: Add and subtract within 1000 with the written column method, carrying and borrowing (incl. across zeros)
points.note: Tuck's regrouping activities model the trade with base-ten blocks; the bridge to the written digits (the carried 1, the crossed-out borrow, the double borrow across a zero) is missing.

points.skill: Know the multiplication tables 2-10 from memory, deriving unknown facts from neighbours
points.note: The meaning of a product is covered; fluency with a table and its structure (each fact is one group more than the last) is not. G3-405 has an empty title line in the input but is 'Times Table of 9' (file G3-405-times-table-of-9.js).

points.skill: Solve multiplication and division word problems by modelling groups vs group size (share vs make groups)
points.note: The meanings exist as bare apparatus; deciding from a STORY which number is the groups and which the size, and whether to multiply or divide, is not taught.

points.skill: Divide with a remainder; the remainder is always smaller than the divisor
points.note: Maple's Bakery uses exact divisions only; leftovers, 'exact or not' and the too-big-remainder error are untaught. (G3-384's number-line face is also reachable on skip-rod's measure-back setting, which shows the leftover gap.)

points.skill: Solve a logic grid from clues (cross out what cannot be, tick what must be)
points.note: A logic-grid mark screen exists on the printable decks (level set #69), but no activity teaches deduction from clues.

points.skill: Name the stages of the water cycle: evaporation, condensation, precipitation, collection
points.note: No science activity of any kind exists in the 204.

points.skill: Name the parts of a flower and what each does
points.note: No plant activity exists.

points.skill: Compare the butterfly and frog life cycles (true of one, the other, or both)
points.note: No life-cycle activity exists.

points.skill: Order the planets from the Sun and sort them into rocky and giant planets
points.note: No space activity exists. Order and sort are one lesson on one apparatus (two settings).

points.skill: Locate the seven continents and five oceans on a world map
points.note: No map activity exists.

points.skill: Group verbs into word fields by meaning and tell close words apart (stroll/dash, glance/stare)
points.note: Shades activities rank intensity within one field; sorting verbs into fields by what they mean (moving vs seeing) is missing.

points.skill: Form person words with a suffix (bake -> baker, run -> runner) and know what they mean
points.note: Sage's Root Garden recognises farmer/teacher as members of a root family; building the person word from the verb (incl. spelling changes) is not taught.

points.skill: Use a known root to choose the right family form for a sentence (bake / baker / baking / baked)
points.note: The family is found, but choosing the form a sentence needs is missing. Shares the word-press apparatus with person-words under a separate setting (two skills, each its own round set).

points.skill: Run a fair test: predict, test, record what happened and draw a conclusion (sink or float)
points.code: NGSS:3-5 SEP (plan and carry out investigations)
points.note: No investigation activity exists; the lab report's free drawing/writing cannot be checked, so the instrument covers predict -> test -> record -> conclude.

points.skill: Trace and copy a sentence in joined (cursive) handwriting
points.note: Print letter tracing exists (penny-alphabet-trace, snippy); joined writing does not. Free copying cannot be checked; the screen traces the joined guide path.

points.skill: Classify by two attributes at once (two-circle Venn, row × column table, the missing cell) (part moved to logic-cabinet)
points.note: Split out by the design review: this worksheet is taught by logic-cabinet.

points.skill: Match words that mean the same; pick a synonym for "said" (part moved to doing-stage)
points.note: Split out by the design review: this worksheet is taught by doing-stage.

points.skill: Yesterday/today/tomorrow, months in order, month before/after, day abbreviations, months and seasons (part moved to season-wheel)
points.note: Split out by the design review: this worksheet is taught by season-wheel.
